hints.title: Daily Gain Scaling
hints.text: When k monsters have already been killed, defeating the next monster with health power takes ceil(power / (k + 1)) days.

hints.title: Subproblem State Definition
hints.text: Since n is at most 17, represent the set of defeated monsters as a bitmask where the i-th bit indicates if monster i is dead.

hints.title: Transitions Over Unvisited Monsters
hints.text: For each state mask, let k be the number of set bits. Try defeating each unvisited monster j to transition to mask | (1 << j).

hints.title: Bitmask Dynamic Programming Implementation

complexity.notes: There are 2^n states, each taking O(n) transitions.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all n! permutation orders is intractable for n up to 17.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bitmask table of size 2^n stores minimum days to reach each subset of defeated monsters.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applies bitmask dynamic programming over permutation subsets to avoid n! factorial search.
